exposure: type of caesarean section (elective vs. emergency)
cohort: The study included 386 mothers who had undergone caesarean sections in two teaching hospitals in Enugu, South-East Nigeria.
finding: Overall, maternal counseling for caesarean section was found to be inadequate in the studied hospitals, with only 41.7% of women receiving adequate counseling.
mod_finding: Women undergoing elective caesarean sections had a significantly higher prevalence of adequate informed consent (67.9%) compared to those undergoing emergency caesarean sections (39.9%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected from mothers in the postnatal wards after their caesarean sections.
